From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ethan Lowe <ethan@parkly.com>
Date: 2028-03-23T10:16:00Z
Subject: Re: Parkly billing — unusual token buckets from Mar 15-17

Folks — I pulled the events and did a preliminary join between request metadata and our cost-classifier. Key findings: 
- 2028-03-15 02:00–06:30 UTC: ~1.2M tokens were classified as long_form_generation because the requests included a large JSON 'context' field that the tokenizer split into multiple segments. Parkly's sample shows big base64 blobs in the payload which inflate tokenizer length.
- 2028-03-16 23:00 UTC: a retry storm (same requestid repeated 3–5x) from one IP was recorded; our dedupe window is 5s and those fell outside it due to slight timestamp drift from Parkly's client.
- No model-side change or billing rule change on our platform during that window.

I've attached our extracted log lines for March 15–17 to help reconcile. There's one suspicious user-agent 'parkly-ingest/1.0 (libsync)' that correlates with the highest-cost requests.

Proposed immediate steps:
1) Provide Parkly a cleaned sample of our classification (attached).
2) Offer a one-time pro-rated credit for duplicates we agree are replays.
3) Recommend Parkly narrow their retry policy and canonicalize timestamps to avoid dedupe misses.

Attachments: redwood_usage_logs_20280315-17.txt

— Ben
Ben Carter
Revenue Ops Analyst
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Lowe <ethan@parkly.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-24T08:51:00Z
Subject: Re: Parkly billing — token classification / bucket mismatch (Mar 15-17)

Ethan — quick note from infra/ops: we ran your sample against the tokenizer split locally. Two things to call out: 
- Embedded binary and escaped JSON increase token counts substantially; in a few examples your payload had repeated log dumps inside the request body. Those are being counted as input tokens per our policy.
- For the repeated requestids, we see a TTL misalignment between Parkly's worker clocks and our ingestion edge which allowed retries to be accepted as distinct requests.

If Parkly wants, we can: 
- Offer a one-time credit covering the deduped portion (~$3,900) while you audit your ingestion;
- Provide a short checklist to reduce token inflation (strip base64 blobs, compress payload, or move large context to an external store and reference by id).

If agreed, Ben can issue the credit and I'll coordinate a short runbook session with your eng team.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Ops Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Ethan Lowe <ethan@parkly.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-28T15:42:00Z
Subject: Re: Parkly billing — token classification / bucket mismatch (Mar 15-17)

Thanks, team — that explanation tracks with our engineering review. We must have started shipping a debug payload with base64 snapshots for a short window and a worker misclock created retries. 

We accept the one-time credit and would like the runbook session next week (Mar 31 or Apr 1). Also, we need the credit note to show the VAT impact so our AP team can apply it against the outstanding invoice. Can you send a PDF credit note and the VAT breakdown?

I'll sign off on the schedule once you propose a time.

Best,
Ethan
Finance Manager
Parkly Inc.
